title: openai-compat: multipart file validation, size limits, and streaming stability for tool/file inputs
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Validate multipart uploads on OpenAI-compat endpoints; enforce per-file and total payload limits; improve streaming stability for multipart file uploads; add metrics and observability for content-type and size rejections.
description: Context: The OpenAI-compat API path accepted multipart file uploads used by tool/function calling and user-provided files. We observed two classes of issues in customer workloads: (1) malformed content-type headers and unsupported multipart boundaries causing 500s, and (2) very large or many small files causing streaming interruptions and OOM pressure on the compat service. Motivation: Improve platform stability and provide clear, consistent errors to downstream callers while maintaining compatibility with existing OpenAI-style clients. Summary of changes: - Add strict content-type validation for multipart/form-data and for individual part content-types; respond with 400 + machine-readable error when invalid. - Enforce configurable per-file and total-payload limits for the OpenAI-compat endpoints (defaults: 50MB per file, 200MB total per request) with clear error codes. - Harden streaming path: add backpressure points, incremental size accounting, and early drain to avoid buffering entire payload. - Update the OpenAI-compat translation layer to produce OpenAI-style error shapes for size/content-type violations. - Add new metrics: multipart.upload.total_size, multipart.upload.file_count, multipart.upload.size_rejected, and multipart.upload.content_type_rejected. - Add unit + integration tests and a small benchmark that simulates concurrent multipart uploads to validate CPU/memory behaviour. Checklist: - [x] content-type validation implemented - [x] per-file and total limits implemented and config-gated - [x] streaming backpressure fixes in handler - [x] OpenAI-compatible error translation for clients - [x] unit and integration tests added - [x] docs snippet in redwood-docs with error shapes Testing notes: Ran full CI (unit + integration + e2e-streaming). CI showed a flaky streaming e2e on first run (connection drop simulated) — fixed by adding an explicit drain and retry on transient socket errors; reran and all checks passed. Load test: simulated 200 concurrent multipart uploads with mixed small and large files; memory stayed within expected SLOs and the 95th latency improved by ~18% relative to previous implementation. Rollout plan: Feature is behind a feature-flag (openai_compat.multipart_validations). Rollout will be gradual: enable for 10% of traffic for 48h, monitor metrics (size_rejected, content_type_rejected, error_rate), then 50% and 100% if stable. Backwards compatibility: Default limits are conservative and config-overridable per-customer for Dedicated/Private deployments. Clients that currently rely on accepting arbitrary content-types will receive a 400; docs updated with guidance. Related: addresses ENG-8421 and PM-317.
